papers.title: Electron paramagnetic resonance spectra and electron spin relaxation of six-coordinate lanthanide complexes with a phosphine oxide ligand
papers.authors: Jacob P. Brannon, Thomas Albrecht, Sandra S. Eaton, Gareth R. Eaton
papers.summary: Pulsed EPR measurements across eight six-coordinate lanthanide complexes reveal shorter phase-memory and relaxation times than in several higher-coordinate analogues. The authors relate rapid dephasing to vibrational modulation of the magnetic anisotropy and identify differences among the metal ions.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A controlled ligand series gives an experimental comparison for lanthanide qubit design.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how coordination around a lanthanide ion affects electron-spin dynamics.

papers.title: Electron paramagnetic resonance spectra and spin relaxation of manganese(III) complexes with Acetylacetonates and pyrophosphate ligands
papers.authors: Surendra Mahapatro, Tanden A. Hovey, Rohan Mansingh, Nina M. Strassner, Thomas Strassner, Ronghe Wang, Mykhaylo Ozerov, Stephen Hill, Sandra S. Eaton, Gareth R. Eaton
papers.summary: High-field spectra resolve the zero-field splitting of two manganese acetylacetonates. Pulsed EPR on these compounds and a pyrophosphate complex gives relaxation times that the authors compare with splitting energies to test a thermally activated relaxation mechanism.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Pairs measured spin lifetimes with a ligand-dependent energy scale that can be varied chemically.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect molecular energy levels and the lattice environment to spin relaxation.

papers.title: Stable Open-Shell Bowl-Shaped Cycloarene with Multiple Hybrid Spin–Spin Coupling and Tunable Radical Characters
papers.authors: Yuanhe Gu, Dongyue An, Tong Shen, Ya Zou, Rong Zhang, Jiangyu Zhu, Teng Wang, Jishan Wu, Yunqi Liu, Xuefeng Lu
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: A bowl-shaped cycloarene combines several radical motifs in a single crystal and binds fullerene guests. Experiments show that an electron-accepting guest changes the coupling among the host spins, providing a chemical handle on its open-shell character.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Guest binding offers a way to tune intramolecular exchange in a stable molecular scaffold.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate how molecular structure stabilizes coupled radical spins.

papers.title: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4 H − SiC
papers.authors: Irene Donà, Michele Segantini, Gianluca Marcozzi, Nguyen Tien Son, Takeshi Ohshima, Ha Duong Ngo, Boris Naydenov
papers.summary: Pulsed EPR distinguishes relaxation and coherence on the central and satellite transitions of silicon vacancies in silicon carbide. The satellite transition gives longer lifetimes at low temperature, and the authors identify nuclear and electron spin diffusion as major dephasing mechanisms.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Transition selection is an experimentally accessible control when comparing coherence measurements.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use transition-selective measurements to characterize addressable electron spins.

papers.title: Suppressing t1-noise in solid-state NMR D-HMQC using spin-echo and dipolar-echo based sequences
papers.authors: Hao Gu, Yury G. Kolyagin, Julien Trébosc, Olivier Lafon, Jean-Paul Amoureux, Lixin Liang, Guangjin Hou
papers.summary: Two echo-based pulse sequences reduce indirect-dimension noise in solid-state correlation NMR. Across experiments and simulations at slow to moderate spinning speeds, dipolar echoes give the greatest tolerance to chemical-shift anisotropy and fluctuations in the spinning rate.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The pulse comparisons isolate two sources of artifacts that can otherwise obscure weak correlations.

relatedPapers.reason: Both compare control sequences by how well they suppress unwanted spin evolution.

papers.title: Optimal dynamical decoupling of a quantum-dot qubit from a phonon bath
papers.summary: For an excitonic qubit in a semiconductor dot, the authors calculate pulse timings tailored to its phonon bath. In their model the optimized timings preserve coherence better than a sequence designed independently of that spectrum.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A concrete example of designing a decoupling sequence from a measured or modeled noise spectrum.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern pulse timing as a means of limiting decoherence.

papers.title: Bridging pulse and circuit levels: a geometric framework for deterministic error suppression
papers.authors: Junkai Zeng, Hao Liang, Yong Ju Hai, Xiu Hao Deng
papers.summary: The authors represent coherent gate errors as trajectories and select twirling gates that cancel their accumulation. Their analysis relates discrete circuit operations to robust pulse design and predicts bounded accumulation for the errors considered.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Connects control at the pulse level with coherent-error cancellation across successive gates.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine deterministic cancellation of control errors.

papers.title: Quantum noise in a squeezed-light-enhanced multiparameter quantum sensor
papers.authors: Aleksandra Sierant, Diana Méndez-Avalos, Santiago Tabares Giraldo, Morgan W. Mitchell
papers.summary: A single atomic ensemble measures a static field and one component of an oscillating field. Varying the polarization noise of squeezed light reveals how measurement backaction and readout noise compete when the magnetometer estimates both quantities.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The experiment separates noise contributions that matter when optimizing two sensing channels simultaneously.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate how the measurement protocol sets sensitivity and systematic limitations.

papers.title: Non-Markovian delay-assisted sensing with waveguide-coupled quantum emitters
papers.authors: Prajit Dhara, Isack Padilla, Saikat Guha, Annyun Das, Kanu Sinha
papers.summary: In a model of two emitters coupled to a waveguide, delayed optical feedback increases the information available about a field gradient. The authors trace the enhancement to prolonged light–emitter interactions and contributions from multiple field modes.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Connects the spatial arrangement of probes to sensitivity in a distributed quantum sensor.

relatedPapers.reason: Both analyze how a sensing protocol changes the information available about a target field.

papers.title: Lanthanide Grafting Modulates Radiative and Nonradiative Energy Dissipation in a Defect-Rich In-MOF for Dual-Functional Luminescence Sensing and Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
papers.authors: Xian Wang, Yi-Qing Miao, Wei-Li Zhai, Jie Duan, Xin-Bin Cai, Wei-Qian Li, Jingjing Chang, Zhi-Gang Wang, Wei Zhu, Qing Li
papers.summary: Grafting europium or terbium onto a defect-rich indium framework creates an optical readout for chromate in water. Spectroscopic measurements implicate competing absorption and changes in coordination in the observed fluorescence quenching.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Offers an experimentally tested recognition and optical readout scheme for ions in porous hosts.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect local framework chemistry to ion-sensitive readout.

papers.title: Machine-learning-assisted tracking of magnetic objects using quantum diamond magnetometry
papers.authors: Fernando Meneses, Christopher T.-K. Lew, Anand Sivamalai, Andy Sayers, Brant C. Gibson, Andrew D. Greentree, Lloyd C. L. Hollenberg, David A. Simpson
papers.summary: A diamond magnetometer records the changing field of a moving elevator. A model trained on experimental signals estimates position along a single axis in real time, providing a test of magnetic tracking without a detailed field model.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The experiment tests position inference under realistic magnetic backgrounds.

relatedPapers.reason: Both consider the relationship between a spin-sensor readout and the quantity inferred from it.

papers.title: Unraveling the Mechanism for Phonon Based Heat Transport in Metal‐Organic Frameworks
papers.authors: Florian P. Lindner, Marco Moser, Lukas Legenstein, Sandro Wieser, Egbert Zojer
papers.summary: Calculations for MOF-5 and HKUST-1 reproduce single-crystal thermal conductivities when they include coupling between closely spaced vibrational bands. The analysis distinguishes low-frequency propagating modes from interband contributions that persist at higher frequencies.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Gives a mechanism to compare with thermal transport measurements on conductive framework crystals.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate which vibrations carry heat in crystalline metal–organic frameworks.

papers.title: Industrial RPCVD growth of high-purity 28Si epilayers with 29Si content below 30 ppm for high-fidelity electron spin qubits
papers.authors: Zhenzhen Kong, Weizhu Liao, Ning Chu, Yiwen Zhang, Ying Zhang, Jixuan Li, Changyang Xu, Yongliang Hao, Yi Zhou, Yanpeng Song, Xiaomeng Liu, Hailing Wang, Xiangsheng Wang, Jinbiao Liu, Chao Zhao, Hao Meng, Gang Cao, Guo-Ping Guo, Hai-Ou Li, Guilei Wang
papers.summary: The authors grow isotopically enriched silicon by reduced-pressure chemical vapor deposition and characterize its isotope content and electronic transport. A double quantum dot fabricated on the film provides spin-echo and gate-fidelity measurements on the same materials platform.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Links measured isotope purity and processing conditions to qubit performance on a fabricated device.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how isotope selection affects the spin environment of a qubit.

papers.title: Shortwave‐Infrared Electrochromic Covalent Organic Framework Supercapacitor for Encapsulation‐Penetrative Energy Storage Monitoring
papers.authors: Yunzhi Qian, Yingfei Wang, Haibing Huang, Qing Hao, Hong Liu
papers.summary: An oriented covalent framework film combines charge storage with a change in shortwave infrared absorption. Imaging the film through an opaque package tracks its state of charge, linking the electronic response of framework units to a device readout.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Shows how an electronic change in a framework electrode can be measured optically during operation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both integrate a framework material into a device and assess its functional response.

papers.title: Optical decoherence in Er3+-doped CeO2 spin qubit platforms
papers.authors: Vrindaa Somjit, Ignas Masiulionis, Gregory D. Grant, Weiguo Jing, Matteo Giantomassi, Supratik Guha, Gian-Marco Rignanese, F. Joseph Heremans, Jiefei Zhang, Giulia Galli
papers.summary: Electronic-structure calculations identify photoionizable cerium polarons as a source of optical decoherence for erbium in ceria. Concentration-dependent photocurrent measurements under resonant illumination support a charge-noise pathway relevant to the optical interface.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Shows how defects in the host can impair the optical coherence of a rare-earth ion.

relatedPapers.reason: Both assess host-dependent optical properties of localized rare-earth centers.

papers.title: First-principles cumulant approach to the vibronic structure of spin defects
papers.authors: Jinsoo Park, Yu Jin, Arpan Kundu, Jorge O. Sofo, Giulia Galli
papers.summary: First-principles calculations for a diamond nitrogen vacancy predict phonon sidebands extending over a broad energy range even at zero temperature. Resolving the coupling by orbital and spin reveals which vibrational modes shape the spectrum.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A microscopic reference for assigning vibronic structure in optical spectra of spin-bearing materials.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how vibrational modes couple differently to specific electronic states.

papers.title: Monomer Flexibility Enables the Regulation of Interlayer Stacking in Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.authors: Xuhan Zheng, Wenqi Qiu, Yuman Guo, Xiudong Wang, Hui Liu, Cheng Gu, Yingjie Zhao
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Across eight imine-linked frameworks, pairs of flexible monomers favor a different stacking arrangement from flexible and rigid pairs. The resulting pore geometries distinguish xylene isomers to different degrees, linking stacking control to a measured separation outcome.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Provides a molecular design variable for controlling registry between adjacent framework layers.

relatedPapers.reason: Both tune ligand properties to control stacking in layered frameworks.

papers.title: Aqueous Synthesis of Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Nanosheets towards Membrane-Based Li+/Mg2+ Separation
papers.authors: Hao Deng, Yong Zhu, Kai Xu, Xiao Pang, Yanqiu Lu, Yu Zheng, Ying Wang, Bohui Lyu, Runnan Zhang, Zhongyi Jiang, Sui Zhang
papers.summary: Reversible aldehyde capping regulates the polymerization rate of ionic framework sheets in water. Repulsion between charged monomers limits stacking, and membranes assembled from the resulting sheets selectively separate lithium from magnesium ions.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Separates the kinetic control of condensation from the electrostatic control of stacking.

relatedPapers.reason: Both control crystallization by adjusting reaction kinetics.

papers.title: COFFlow: Building-Block-Based Generative Modeling for Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework Discovery
papers.authors: Yuanhui Pan, Yunrui Yan, Cheng Zeng, Jirui Jin, Mingjie Liu
papers.summary: A generative model assembles periodic two-dimensional frameworks from molecular building blocks. Tests include unseen blocks and topologies, and a methane-storage screen identifies candidate structures while revealing where chemical validity deteriorates during extrapolation.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Validity tests help prioritize computationally proposed frameworks for structural review before synthesis.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use computational screening to evaluate framework structures.
